Why this method:
- In [`PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldComparison`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java:889 ), the method immediately rejects most comparisons unless both operands satisfy `NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(..., false)`. `NodeUtil.isLiteralValue` does not treat `Token.NOT` expressions like `!0` and `!1` as literals, even though [`NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java:119 ) can evaluate them as pure booleans.
- That explains `x = !1 == !0` staying unchanged: both sides are boolean constants in effect, but `tryFoldComparison` bails out before folding equality.
- The same method also handles `undefined` asymmetrically. In the `Token.NAME` branch, it only recognizes left-side `undefined` if `rightLiteral` is true; see the check around [`tryFoldComparison`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java:1030 ). Since `rightLiteral` is false for `!0`, `undefined == !0` does not fold, while the commuted form can take a different path. That matches the commutativity failure.
- By contrast, `!0 > undefined` can fold to `false` through the `undefinedRight` path and [`compareToUndefined`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java:1121 ), which is why the invertibility test sees inconsistent behavior across equivalent expressions.

m23.content:
Static diagnosis points to `com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldComparison(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)` as the buggy method.

Why this method:
- In [`PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldComparison`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java:889 ), the method immediately rejects most comparisons unless both operands satisfy `NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(..., false)`. `NodeUtil.isLiteralValue` does not treat `Token.NOT` expressions like `!0` and `!1` as literals, even though [`NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/NodeUtil.java:119 ) can evaluate them as pure booleans.
- That explains `x = !1 == !0` staying unchanged: both sides are boolean constants in effect, but `tryFoldComparison` bails out before folding equality.
- The same method also handles `undefined` asymmetrically. In the `Token.NAME` branch, it only recognizes left-side `undefined` if `rightLiteral` is true; see the check around [`tryFoldComparison`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java:1030 ). Since `rightLiteral` is false for `!0`, `undefined == !0` does not fold, while the commuted form can take a different path. That matches the commutativity failure.
- By contrast, `!0 > undefined` can fold to `false` through the `undefinedRight` path and [`compareToUndefined`]( /abs/path/com/google/javascript/jscomp/PeepholeFoldConstants.java:1121 ), which is why the invertibility test sees inconsistent behavior across equivalent expressions.

Dynamic verification was inconclusive because the nominated lines were not reached in the debugger, so this diagnosis is based on static control-flow and the failing test patterns. The defect is still specific: comparison folding is using the wrong notion of “foldable constant” and has asymmetric `undefined` handling for `NAME` operands.
